business_model.claim: Overview: The business monetizes professional hockey through tickets, concessions and merchandise, media rights, sponsorships, signage, suites, and league distributions. Customers include fans, suite licensees, sponsors and broadcasters. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, event-related revenue was $5.176 million, sponsorship/signage/suites $4.123 million, league distributions and other $2.950 million, and media rights $1.840 million (10-Q, L761–767; revenue definitions at L775–777).

recent_developments.claim: The separation completed on October 26, 2026, after the reported quarter (10-Q, L1478). Subsequent liquidity included a $19.095 million cash contribution in October and $40.905 million of collections related to deferred suite and sponsorship revenue following separation (10-Q, L1481). These receipts improve funding but are not evidence of newly earned revenue.
recent_developments.quote: the information set forth in this section also focuses on the liquidity and capital resources of the Company following the Rangers Distribution.

recent_developments.claim: Most important disclosed risk: Personnel and overhead costs can overwhelm modest revenue growth. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, SG&A increased 26% to $28.088 million, including $3.554 million of separation expenses and $1.358 million of higher compensation and benefits (10-Q, L1447). Direct operating expenses increased 145% to $8.802 million, including $3.064 million of additional personnel-transaction provisions (10-Q, L1425–1434). Separation costs and season-start timing explain part of the deterioration, so the quarter should not be treated as a normalized expense run rate.
recent_developments.quote: Selling, general and administrative expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased $5,802, or 26%, to $28,088 as compared to the prior year period primarily driven by expenses related to the Distribution of $3,554 and higher employee compensation and related benefits of $1,358.

limitations: Historical results are carve-out statements, not an observed standalone operating history. Management says actual standalone costs cannot practicably be quantified (10-Q, L703–716).
Seasonality limits annualization: revenue is disproportionately earned during the fiscal second and third quarters, when most games are played (10-Q, L1515–1516).

Attendance, ticket renewal rates, customer counts, market share and quantified pricing power are not stated in the supplied filings; franchise reputation alone does not establish competitive superiority.

Remaining performance obligations exclude contracts originally lasting one year or less and specified variable consideration, so they are neither a complete revenue forecast nor a measure of cash already collected (10-Q, L805–807).
Regional sports-network solvency and affiliate performance are disclosed risks, but their potential financial impact is not quantified in the supplied material (10-Q, L1312 and L1322).
The supplied filing references a separate Information Statement for additional risk factors; that document was not supplied and was not used.

investment_advisor_output.thesis: Contracted revenue visibility and the new rental stream do not yet offset deteriorating operating performance. Reduce exposure until the next filing demonstrates that year-over-year operating-loss deterioration has stopped, while recognizing that seasonal carve-out results are not a normalized standalone earnings baseline.
investment_advisor_output.deciding_number_source: Both analyst outputs cite the year-over-year increase in operating-loss magnitude for the three months ended September 30, 2026: 10-Q, accession 0001628280-26-071325, L1451.
investment_advisor_output.rationale:
Investment Recommendation: Sell. The sole deciding number is the 84% widening in operating loss: modest revenue growth did not translate into improved operating economics. Both analysts agree on that deterioration; the Research Analyst emphasizes contractual visibility and catalysts, while the Financial Analyst emphasizes weak profitability and cash generation. Those perspectives differ in emphasis rather than factual conclusion.

Criterion scores — all filing references below are to 10-Q accession 0001628280-26-071325:
• Earnings strength: 1/5. Revenue grew 3%, but operating loss widened 84% (L1394–1403; L1451). The Financial Analyst calculated an operating margin of −167.42% from revenue and operating loss (L583–592). Operating cash outflow was $71.188 million; negative operating cash flow and negative net income make the positive conversion quotient misleading (L629–633; L648).
• Catalyst credibility: 3/5. The training-center lease provides $2 million of first-contract-year fixed rent, but its net earnings benefit after changes in historical cost allocations is unquantified (L1164–1174).
• Valuation attractiveness: 3/5, a neutral procedural placeholder, not an evidence-based valuation assessment. No price, compatible annual earnings, or comparable peer-period figures were supplied; no supporting valuation number or original filing source exists. Missing inputs establish neither cheapness nor expensiveness.
• Risk-and-reward balance: 2/5. The strongest operating downside is the 84% widening in operating loss (L1451); the strongest contractual positive is $287.741 million of remaining performance obligations (L808–814), which supports visibility but not assured profitability.

The score average is 2.25/5, implying Sell under the prescribed rule, with no recommendation override. This is an operating-evidence recommendation, not a conclusion that the shares are overvalued.

Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations: Monitor realization of the contracted rental stream, standalone overhead, and whether ticket and sponsorship performance supplements league distributions. Avoid annualizing the seasonal quarter. Change the recommendation to Hold if the next filing shows that year-over-year GAAP operating-loss widening has stopped; that would invalidate the main numerical basis for Sell, without by itself establishing attractive valuation.
risks: Main downside risk: Personnel and overhead costs may continue to overwhelm revenue growth; separation expenses and season-start timing explain part, but not necessarily all, of the deterioration.
Historical carve-out statements and centralized cash management do not establish normalized standalone costs or liquidity.
Operating cash consumption and weak reported liquidity create funding risk, although subsequent receipts and available borrowing capacity provide mitigation.
Seasonality and working-capital movements could make the reported deterioration less persistent than the Sell thesis assumes.
Remaining performance obligations are not a complete revenue forecast or cash already collected, and the rental catalyst's net earnings contribution is unquantified.
Missing price and peer information prevents assessing whether the operating risks are already reflected in valuation.
